## `src/bindings/context.rs`

The per-worker MLX bindings context: its submission stream and the linked version.

The context holds exactly the bindings-owned state (which stream work is submitted to, which upstream version is linked), while embedding policy — memory limits and the metallib path selection — stays with the embedding application, which composes this context.

### `MlxBindingsContext`

```rust
pub struct MlxBindingsContext
```

Process-global official MLX C bindings context configured for one worker.

### `MlxBindingsContext::new`

```rust
pub fn new() -> Result<Self, MlxCError>
```

Creates the context after the non-terminating error handler is installed: reads the linked version and acquires the default GPU stream.

### `MlxBindingsContext::on_cpu`

```rust
pub fn on_cpu() -> Result<Self, MlxCError>
```

Creates a context whose submissions target the default CPU stream.

MLX implements several families only on the CPU, including matrix factorization, inversion, and solving, and its GPU backend rejects float64. Every wrapper submits to its context's stream, so those families are reachable only through a context built here.

### `MlxBindingsContext::on_stream`

```rust
pub fn on_stream(stream: MlxStream) -> Result<Self, MlxCError>
```

Creates a context whose submissions target `stream`, such as one from `MlxStream::on_device`. Streams are thread affine unless built through `MlxStream::new_thread_unsafe`, so use this context on the thread that created the stream.

### `MlxBindingsContext::stream`

```rust
pub const fn stream(&self) -> &MlxStream
```

The stream every submission from this context targets.

### `MlxBindingsContext::gpu_stream`

```rust
pub const fn gpu_stream(&self) -> &MlxStream
```

The submission stream under its original name, which is the GPU stream unless the context was built through `on_cpu` or `on_stream`; prefer `stream`.

### `MlxBindingsContext::version`

```rust
pub fn version(&self) -> &str
```

The linked upstream MLX version.

## `src/error.rs`

Captured MLX-C error translation.

MLX C reports an error immediately before returning nonzero on the same calling thread, so the capture machinery pairs those two observations thread-locally. This module only translates what MLX-C reported; typed classification of embedding-specific error markers (for example an active memory ceiling) is embedding policy: the consumer converts `MlxCError` values at its own boundary.

Payload trampolines cannot return Rust errors across the C ABI, so they park their typed failure in a separate thread-local slot and return nonzero; status translation prefers that parked failure because it is the root cause, while MLX-C's status text only reports that a callback errored.

### `MlxCError`

```rust
pub struct MlxCError {
    /// The attempted operation, phrased the way runtime error reports name it.
    pub operation: &'static str,
    /// The description MLX-C reported, or a fallback when it reported none.
    pub description: String,
}
```

One failed MLX-C operation: what was attempted and what MLX-C reported.

### `install_non_terminating_error_handler`

```rust
pub fn install_non_terminating_error_handler()
```

Installs the non-terminating MLX-C error handler exactly once per process.

The handler must be installed before any fallible MLX-C call so failures carry descriptions instead of bare nonzero statuses.

### `check_status`

```rust
pub fn check_status(status: i32, operation: &'static str) -> Result<(), MlxCError>
```

Translates an MLX-C status into `Ok(())` or a captured `MlxCError`.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description for the calling thread when the status is nonzero, with a fallback description when MLX-C reported none.

### `take_captured_mlx_error`

```rust
pub fn take_captured_mlx_error() -> Option<String>
```

Takes the captured MLX-C error description for the calling thread, if any.

### `clear_captured_mlx_error`

```rust
pub fn clear_captured_mlx_error()
```

Discards the captured MLX-C error description for the calling thread.

```rust
pub fn set_closure_error(failure: MlxCError)
```
